web_evidence.title: Edge of Eternity — First Chapter
web_evidence.note: The authorized 16-page first chapter sustains third-person narration around Rebecca Hoffmann, repeatedly naming her as she and accessing her memories, perceptions, and thoughts without a participating narrator.

web_evidence.title: Edge of Eternity | Penguin Random House Secondary Education
web_evidence.note: The publisher's extended opening excerpt independently confirms sustained third-person narration and close focalization through Rebecca; it reproduces the same opening represented by the author-hosted chapter.

search_log: Searched “Ken Follett Edge of Eternity official excerpt chapter 1” and publisher/Google Books variants; found authorized excerpts on Ken Follett's site and Penguin Random House.
Opened and inspected the full 16-page author-hosted first-chapter PDF, including its opening, middle, and concluding pages.
Opened the Penguin Random House excerpt and verified that its sustained prose uses the same third-person opening.
Searched the title with “point of view,” “third person,” “narrator,” and “first person”; results supplied no credible contrary first- or second-person description.

Searched the title with “alternating narration,” “multiple narrators,” “epistolary,” “diary,” and “frame narrative”; results described multiple focal characters but provided no evidence of grammatical-person alternation or an epistolary frame.
Opened Google Books, but its accessible page offered bibliographic data and a keyword index rather than a sustained interior passage.
Discarded false positives for the unrelated same-title religious novel and the Edge of Eternity video game.
person_note: The controlling narration is third person with shifting focal characters. The authorized opening follows Rebecca externally while entering her thoughts, and interior Goodreads passages independently show the same technique with Jasper and Walli. First-person language in the quote set belongs to dialogue, speeches, aphorisms, or local thought rather than a participating narrator; generic you likewise does not create second-person narration. Searches found descriptions of numerous viewpoint characters but no credible evidence that any sustained section changes grammatical person. Web prose coverage is limited to the opening, but several separated interior quote passages corroborate it, supporting high confidence.
